text:
sasha: heads up — saw a 2.3x p99 token latency spike in prod after yesterday's batching handoff change. TL;DR: adaptive batcher now hands off to the microkernel more aggressively and we see a lot of tiny kernel launches in the nsys traces.
kevin: ouch, do you have an example trace?
sasha: pasted nsys output to the artifacts bucket: gs://redwood-prof/traces/1749001234/nsys_run1.qdrep, also uploaded perfetto capture (perfetto://1749001234/pft). main hotspots are a flurry of `attention_fwd` kernels and `kv_cache_load` calls each <200us.
marta: can you paste the timeline snippet? it's easier to see the launch overhead.
sasha: sure — timeline excerpt:
```
0.00s - prepare batch
0.04s - attention_fwd (0.12ms)
0.04s - kv_cache_load (0.09ms)
0.05s - attention_fwd (0.14ms)
0.06s - attention_fwd (0.11ms)
0.06s - cudaMemcpy (0.02ms)
0.07s - kernel launch overhead (0.08ms)
```
kevin: that pattern screams too-small microbatches and thrashing of kernel selector. Did the change alter the handoff token threshold?
sasha: yes — in batcher_hotpath.cpp we lowered handoff_threshold from 64 -> 32 to try to reduce tail latency for short requests. commit abc1234e changed that.
perf-bot: automated bisect candidate: commit abc1234e suspected (range: def000..ghi999) — reproduced locally on h100-dev-02 with small sequence workloads.
marta: interestingly, on A100 the overhead is smaller but still visible. on H100 the kernel launch and scheduling latency seems amplified because the microkernel path creates many short kernels instead of fusing ops.
kevin: do we have a reproducer script? I can run a tighter loop and capture nsys + nvtx spans.
sasha: added run_repro.py to the trace artifacts — it emits the same seq distribution and logs timestamps. use: `python run_repro.py --model gpt-small --seqs 4-64 --iters 500`
kevin: i'll run nsys with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,env --output=run1 ./run_repro.py ...` and also collect a perfetto for timeline.
marta: quick grep in the trace shows kernel names: `attention_fwd`, `kv_cache_lookup`, `softmax_fwd`, several <300us. NVTX spans show back-to-back launches with <50us gaps.
kevin: hypothesis: reducing handoff threshold increased frequency of microkernel selection which breaks kernel fusion opportunities in the compiler/kernelselector. more launches -> higher relative syscall/context cost.
sasha: agreed. Also seeing more `cuLaunchKernel` overhead clusters in the nsys API trace.
perf-bot: note: quantization path unaffected — the spike is in FP16 fused kernels only.
kevin: plan: 1) reproduce on both H100/A100 VMs, 2) bisect more precisely around abc1234e to confirm causality, 3) run a compile+kernel selection trace (enable KERNEL_SELECTOR_DEBUG=1) to capture decision logs.
marta: another idea: add hysteresis to handoff so we don't flip to microkernel for sequences that are near the threshold. e.g., require 3 consecutive small-batch occurrences before switching.
sasha: +1 on hysteresis. also add aggregation window to prefer fusion when total tokens in flight across requests > X.
kevin: i'm starting a bisect now — if it points at abc1234e, propose reverting threshold change and adding a unit perf test for kernel fusion counts.
infra-bot: scheduled n1-standard-32 h100 instances for kevin (h100-dev-02) for 2h starting now.
kevin: ran bisect step 1 -> abc1234e reproduces the spike locally. bisect narrowed to abc1234e as the breaking change.
marta: can we get a before/after flamegraph? even aggregated kernel time per request would help.
sasha: uploaded two flamegraphs: gs://redwood-prof/fg/before_1748900000.svg and gs://redwood-prof/fg/after_1749001234.svg — after shows many small peaks instead of 1 fused block.
kevin: run nvprof just to double-check kernel launch overhead numbers: nvprof shows average kernel launch cost ~60-90us during spike window.
marta: action items: Sasha — open PR to revert threshold + add hysteresis prototype; Kevin — add KERNEL_SELECTOR_DEBUG traces and perf test asserting fused-kernel count >= N for typical batch shapes; Sasha/Keving — run A/B on staging with canary traffic.
sasha: I made a draft revert branch `revert/hand-off-threshold-1749001234`, will open PR with profiling artifacts attached.
kevin: adding a telemetry metric to console: `kernel_launch_count_per_request` and `fused_kernel_blocks_per_request`. we can roll metrics to detect regressions.
marta: also add an integration test that runs the reproducer for 100 iters and asserts p99 tokens < baseline*1.2.
perf-bot: reminder: attach nsight/qdrep + perfetto to PRs for quick review.
sasha: thanks all — will push PR and ping #eng-runtime. if revert looks good, we can rework the heuristic with hysteresis and a default threshold back to 64. :thumbsup:
kevin: will follow up with H100 vs A100 microbench numbers tomorrow.
infra-bot: logs archived to gs://redwood-prof/archives/1749001234/ (nsys, perfetto, nvprof, flamegraphs).
marta: marking as triaged — moving to a short-term hotfix.
sasha: I'll post PR link when ready and drop final before/after timelines.
kevin: thanks, everyone.
